findings.title: Production Hostinger FTP password committed in plaintext and still present in git history; never rotated
findings.status: MITIGATED — PASSWORD ROTATED / RESIDUAL HISTORY OPEN
findings.evidence: git show e8e358a^:zankurd_mobile/deploy_ftp.sh lines 3-5 contain literal production credentials: HOST="82.25.***.***", USER="u6226*****.zankurd.com", PASS="Amargi.***REDACTED***", used at line 20 as --user "$USER:$PASS". The project's own commit body for e8e358a (2026-07-24) states: 'deploy_ftp.sh içindeki açık metin FTP şifresi kaldırıldı... Not: Sızan FTP şifresi git GEÇMİŞİNDE hâlâ mevcut — Hostinger'dan şifre değiştirilmeli.' (The leaked FTP password is still in git HISTORY — the password must be changed at Hostinger.)
findings.expected: No production credential appears in any commit
findings.actual: HEAD is clean (deploy_ftp.sh now delegates to deploy_sftp.sh and reads secrets from the gitignored .env.deploy), but the credential remains reachable in history
findings.impact: This account hosts zankurd.com, which serves the privacy policy, terms of use and account-deletion pages that both stores require. Compromise would allow those legally-required pages to be altered or removed and malicious content to be served on the web build.
findings.policy_reference: n/a (security); indirectly affects the integrity of the Privacy Policy / Support / Account Deletion URLs declared to both stores
findings.root_cause: The deploy script originally embedded credentials. Fixed on 2026-07-24 but forward-only: history was not rewritten and the password was not rotated.
findings.mitigating_fact: git remote -v shows origin is a LOCAL bundle file (/Users/kocer/Downloads/zankurd-mac-aktarim.bundle), not GitHub or any public remote. The repository has never been pushed publicly, so present exposure is limited to those with access to the local filesystem and that 167 MB bundle. This lowers, but does not remove, the severity.
findings.remediation: Order matters. (1) Rotate the password at Hostinger FIRST — this is the only real fix; scrubbing history is useless while the credential stays live. (2) Move to SFTP/key-based access only (HEAD already delegates to deploy_sftp.sh). (3) Before the repo is ever made public, scrub history with git filter-repo and destroy the bundle. (4) Keep the new secret only in .env.deploy and GitHub Actions secrets — the workflow already correctly uses ${{ secrets.HOSTINGER_FTP_* }}.
findings.validation: Password-change record in the Hostinger panel; git log --all -S'<old-password>' returns 0 results after scrubbing; successful deploy via deploy_sftp.sh
findings.auditor_note: Missed on the first pass because the history scan was filename-based (*.env*, key.properties, *.jks, *.p8) while the secret lived inside a shell script. Name-based scanning is insufficient without content-based search (git log -S).
findings.phase2_update: 2026-08-02 (Phase 2): Owner confirmed the Hostinger password was rotated. Local verification (SHA-256 comparison, no values printed): .env.deploy contains NO password field at all — deployment moved to SSH key auth (SFTP_IDENTITY_FILE); the old credential is absent from .env.deploy and from all tracked files -> DIFFERENT (superseded). deploy_ftp.sh is now a 6-line shim exec'ing deploy_sftp.sh (BatchMode, IdentitiesOnly, StrictHostKeyChecking, pinned known_hosts). The .github/workflows/deploy-web-hostinger.yml that referenced FTP_PASSWORD no longer exists. ACTIVE credential risk is mitigated; the historical commit record remains and history scrub is deliberately deferred to a separate backed-up phase.
history_locations: zankurd_mobile/deploy_ftp.sh:3-5 (commit e8e358a^ ve öncesi) — parola satır içi
/.env.deploy (depo KÖKÜ, commit c8a2001'de eklendi, sonra silindi) — FTP_HOST/USER/PASS/REMOTE, 101 bayt
findings.history_scrub_note: 2026-08-02 doğrulaması: sızan parola geçmişte İKİ ayrı yolda duruyor, tek yolda değil. Her ikisindeki FTP_PASS değeri aynı (sha256 018bd779…) ve o parola sahip tarafından döndürüldü, yani kalıntı artık kullanılamaz bir sırdır. Ancak ileride git-history temizliği yapılırken YALNIZ deploy_ftp.sh temizlenirse kökteki .env.deploy blob'u geride kalır. filter-repo çağrısı iki yolu da kapsamalıdır. Bugünkü .env.deploy ile tek çakışan alan FTP_HOST (sunucu adresi); parola ve kullanıcı farklı, dağıtım da SSH anahtarına geçmiş durumda.

findings.title: Android release binary cannot be produced — signing material absent
findings.evidence: flutter build appbundle --release and flutter build apk --release both exit 1 with: 'Release signing configuration is missing or incomplete. Expected android/key.properties with non-empty fields: storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias, keyPassword ... The release build was stopped for security and will not fall back to debug signing.'
findings.expected: Signed app-release.aab is produced
findings.actual: Gradle throws GradleException, exit code 1
findings.impact: No AAB can be uploaded to Google Play. Also blocks: release bundle size measurement, R8 output review, merged release manifest inspection, and 16 KB verification from the release binary itself.
findings.policy_reference: Google Play upload requirement; Play App Signing
findings.root_cause: Upload keystore and android/key.properties are intentionally not stored in the repository and are absent on this machine. The gradle gate is correct behaviour — it refuses to silently fall back to debug signing.
findings.remediation: Owner restores/creates the upload keystore and a local android/key.properties (never committed). If Play App Signing is enabled, only the upload key is required.
findings.validation: flutter build appbundle --release -> exit 0; then bundletool build-apks + zipalign -c -P 16 + llvm-readelf -lW on release .so files
findings.phase2_update: 2026-08-02 (Phase 2): New RSA-4096 upload keystore created at ~/.zankurd/signing/zankurd-upload.jks (alias zankurd-upload, SHA384withRSA, valid to 2056-07-25), password held in macOS Keychain (round-trip verified), android/key.properties written mode 600 and confirmed gitignored + untracked. Signed release AAB produced: 73,530,129 B, SHA-256 175147659c5177cc7d2fb611bd27fe87d5427751f1ae2be5f4df01a5c75f07bf. jarsigner -> 'jar verified'; signer cert SHA-256 80:59:2E:...:98:B3 matches the upload key; zero 'Android Debug' occurrences; bundletool validate passed; targetSdk/compileSdk 36, minSdk 24; R8 ran (mapping.txt 295,909 lines). Installs and launches on Android 16 with zero FATAL/E-flutter/dlopen errors. NOTE: shippability is tracked separately as P1-005.

findings.title: iPad is a declared supported device but the iPad layout is unfinished (stretched phone UI)
findings.status: FIXED — content now constrained to 820pt; bespoke tablet layout remains a design choice, not a defect
findings.evidence: Real iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator, iOS 26.5. Onboarding: hero card becomes a ~1400pt-wide empty green rectangle with a small centred icon, followed by ~400pt of dead space. Name gate: full-width orange header with content compressed into the left ~30%, a small centred card, and ~600pt of empty space below. Root cause is visible in source: ResponsiveWrapper caps content at maxContentWidth = 1200 and only activates above wideThreshold = 600; iPad Pro 13-inch portrait logical width is ~1032pt, so the 1200pt cap never binds.
findings.reproduction: flutter build ios --simulator --debug; xcrun simctl boot <iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)>; xcrun simctl install <udid> build/ios/iphonesimulator/Runner.app; xcrun simctl launch <udid> com.zankurd.app; xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot out.png
findings.expected: On iPad the content is constrained to a readable measure or uses a tablet-appropriate layout
findings.actual: Phone layout stretched across 1032pt with large empty regions
findings.impact: iPad users see an unfinished, amateur-feeling layout with large empty areas.
findings.policy_reference: App Store Review Guideline 4.0 (Design) / 2.4.1; iPad screenshots are mandatory when the device family includes iPad
findings.root_cause: ResponsiveWrapper was written for desktop web widths only. Its own class documentation records the deferral: 'Gerçek iki sütunlu tablet düzeni kapsamlı bir tasarım işi; izole bir sprint olarak planlanmalı (M-12).'
findings.remediation: Either (a) add a tablet breakpoint reducing maxContentWidth to ~700-820pt, which is small and low-risk and keeps iPad support; or (b) set TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1" to ship iPhone-only and remove the iPad screenshot obligation. This is a product decision for the owner.
findings.validation: Re-run the screen tour on iPad Pro 13-inch, iPad mini and iPad Air simulators; flutter test with no regressions
findings.phase2_update: Deliberately out of scope for Phase 2. Unchanged.

findings.title: Question-quality gate fails (exit 1) — CI is red and real content regressions would be masked
findings.evidence: dart run tool/question_quality/question_quality_audit.dart gate -> 'question-quality: sources=5 reportPhysical=1832 reportCanonical=1771 gatePhysical=1832 gateCanonical=1771 unknown=0' followed by 'Gate source fingerprint changed; baseline metrics were not accepted.' exit 1. SHA-256 comparison against baseline.json: community_questions.json CHANGED, editorial_questions.json CHANGED, offline_questions.json CHANGED; sentence_building_questions.json MATCH; curated_question_bank.dart MATCH.
findings.expected: Gate exits 0 and only fails on genuine content regressions
findings.actual: Gate exits 1 on every run; a genuine regression would produce the same error and be indistinguishable
findings.impact: The CI step that protects question quality no longer discriminates. Pre-release 'CI green' verification is impossible.
findings.policy_reference: Internal release gate (CI step 'Check question quality regressions')
findings.root_cause: Commit e6cb01b (2026-08-01, 'fix(sorular): cevap konumu yanlılığını...') modified three question JSON files. baseline.json was last refreshed at commit c901521 (2026-07-31), i.e. before that content change. Content was fixed; the baseline was not refreshed.
findings.remediation: After reviewing the new content, refresh fingerprints and metrics via the tool's baseline mode. This is safe because the shipped bank currently reports 0 blockers and 0 criticals.
findings.validation: dart run tool/question_quality/question_quality_audit.dart gate -> exit 0
findings.phase2_update: 2026-08-02 (Phase 2): Verified the three changed sources are the documented 2026-08-01 answer-position rebalance + distractor-language fix: 1779->1779 records, 0 added, 0 deleted, only the 'answers' field changed in 1033 records, 0 prompt-text changes, 0 correctAnswer-text changes; 51 records had option content substituted (documented distractor-language fix) with correctAnswer text unchanged in 51/51 and the correct answer still present in 51/51. Baseline refreshed with the tool's own --accept-current-debt mode: delta 'blockers 0->0, criticals 0->0, issues 1856->1856'; baseline.json diff is exactly 3 source fingerprints and the issueFingerprints SET is identical. Question sources untouched. gate -> exit 0 'no regression from baseline'.

findings.title: Advertising ID is collected via Firebase Analytics — store declarations must be reconciled
findings.status: FIXED — AD_ID and Privacy Sandbox permissions removed via tools:node=remove
findings.evidence: aapt2 dump badging on the built APK lists uses-permission com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID, android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION and android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID, none of which appear in the app's own AndroidManifest.xml. On iOS, GoogleAdsOnDeviceConversion.framework is embedded in Runner.app/Frameworks. Meanwhile the published terms.html states the game is free with no ads.
findings.expected: Declared data collection matches what the binary actually collects
findings.actual: Advertising ID capability ships in the binary; the Data Safety / App Privacy answers for it are not yet settled and public terms say 'no ads'
findings.impact: Mismatch between declaration and binary. If the app's target audience includes children, transmitting the Advertising ID is a Play Families policy violation.
findings.policy_reference: Google Play Data Safety (support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469); Apple App Privacy
findings.root_cause: firebase_analytics pulls in ad-attribution components by default via manifest merging and pod dependencies.
findings.remediation: Either declare Advertising ID in Play Data Safety (and keep terms consistent), or remove it: add tools:node="remove" for com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID in the manifest and configure Analytics without ad-id/ads-on-device-conversion.
findings.validation: Re-run aapt2 dump badging and confirm the permission set; confirm the iOS framework list

findings.title: Native debug symbols are not configured for the release bundle
findings.evidence: grep for 'debugSymbolLevel' and 'ndk {' in zankurd_mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts returns no matches, while the APK ships native libraries (libflutter.so, libdartjni.so, libdatastore_shared_counter.so) for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64.
findings.expected: Native debug symbols are generated and uploadable to Play
findings.actual: No symbol configuration; Play Console will warn that debug symbols were not uploaded
findings.impact: Native crashes are reported unsymbolicated, making engine/plugin crashes hard to diagnose in production.
findings.policy_reference: Google Play Console native debug symbols guidance
findings.root_cause: Default Flutter Android template does not configure debugSymbolLevel.
findings.remediation: Add android { buildTypes { release { ndk { debugSymbolLevel = "FULL" } } } }, or build with --split-debug-info and upload the symbols.
findings.validation: Build the release AAB and confirm BUNDLE-METADATA contains native debug symbols

findings.title: 16 KB page-size compatibility not verified on a real 16 KB device
findings.evidence: Emulator reports Android 16 / API 36 / arm64-v8a but 'getconf PAGE_SIZE' returns 4096. The only installed system image is android-36/google_apis/arm64-v8a; no 16 KB page-size image is present. Static ELF proof is strong: release libflutter.so p_align=0x10000; libdartjni.so and libdatastore_shared_counter.so p_align=0x4000; zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4 reports 'Verification successful'.
findings.expected: App launches and runs on a device whose PAGE_SIZE is 16384
findings.actual: No 16 KB environment available; runtime behaviour unverified
findings.impact: Static alignment is necessary but not sufficient; a runtime check would confirm no plugin misbehaves under 16 KB paging.
findings.root_cause: 16 KB system image not installed in the local SDK.
findings.remediation: Install a 16 KB page-size system image, boot it, confirm getconf PAGE_SIZE = 16384, install the release APK and exercise the main flows.
findings.validation: adb shell getconf PAGE_SIZE -> 16384 and a clean launch with no native loader errors in logcat

findings.title: integration_test suite was not executed on a device and is not run by CI
findings.evidence: integration_test/app_flows_test.dart and integration_test/performance_test.dart exist. .github/workflows/flutter_ci.yml runs only 'flutter test --coverage', which does not execute integration tests on a device.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the CI workflow and the integration_test directory
findings.expected: End-to-end flows are exercised on a device at least before release
findings.actual: Never run in CI; not run in this audit
findings.impact: End-to-end regressions can reach a release build undetected.

findings.validation: flutter test integration_test -d <device> -> pass

findings.title: CI builds only a debug APK — the release path (R8, ProGuard, shrinking, signing) is never exercised
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/flutter_ci.yml job build-android runs 'flutter build apk --debug' and uploads app-debug.apk. There is no release build step.
findings.expected: The release code path is compiled at least once per change
findings.actual: Only the debug path is compiled
findings.impact: R8/ProGuard stripping errors, resource-shrinking breakage and release-only crashes are only discoverable by hand.
findings.root_cause: Release signing secrets are not available to CI, so the release build was omitted entirely.
findings.remediation: Add an unsigned or fake-signed release assemble step (e.g. flutter build apk --release with a CI-only debug keystore, or gradle assembleRelease with signing disabled) so R8 runs in CI.
findings.validation: CI job completes the release compile step

findings.title: Firebase native auto-collection is not suppressed, so measurement can start despite consent defaulting to off
findings.evidence: Custom events are correctly gated: main.dart:207 wraps AnalyticsService.instance.initialize() in 'if (analyticsConsentProvider.enabled)'. However, no FIREBASE_ANALYTICS_COLLECTION_ENABLED key exists in ios/Runner/Info.plist or android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (grep returns nothing). The Firebase Analytics native SDK defaults to enabled once Firebase.initializeApp() runs and auto-collects first_open, session_start and app_open. AnalyticsService.disable() (analytics_service.dart:31-40) is only invoked when a user REVOKES consent, never at startup when consent was never granted.
findings.expected: On a fresh install with consent off, no analytics events leave the device
findings.actual: Firebase's automatically-collected events are not suppressed on a fresh install
findings.impact: Contradicts the app's own stated opt-in posture and the published privacy policy. Affects Apple App Privacy and Play Data Safety answers.
findings.policy_reference: Apple App Privacy; Google Play Data Safety
findings.root_cause: Native auto-collection defaults to on and must be disabled declaratively in the platform manifests; only the Dart-side custom-event path was gated.
findings.remediation: Add FIREBASE_ANALYTICS_COLLECTION_ENABLED=false to both platform manifests and call setAnalyticsCollectionEnabled(true) only after consent is granted.
findings.validation: Fresh install with consent off; confirm via Firebase DebugView / network capture that no analytics events are sent

findings.title: Paywall empty state ships a 'Premium packages are not active yet' coming-soon placeholder
findings.evidence: lib/src/l10n/strings.dart:1745 defines 'tr': 'Premium paketler henüz aktif değil'. lib/src/screens/paywall_screen.dart:17 documents this as a user-friendly 'yakında' (coming soon) view shown when RevenueCat returns no offerings.
findings.reproduction: Open the paywall with RevenueCat returning no offerings
findings.expected: The only monetization surface always shows purchasable packages
findings.actual: It can render a coming-soon placeholder
findings.impact: If a reviewer reaches this state, the app presents an unfinished feature.
findings.policy_reference: App Store Review Guideline 2.1 / 4.2 (minimum functionality, incomplete features)
findings.root_cause: Empty-state fallback when the offerings fetch is empty or fails. AppConfig.validateForRelease already forces RevenueCat keys to be present in release builds, so the risk is dashboard configuration rather than a missing key.
findings.remediation: Confirm the 'premium' entitlement and at least one offering are live in the RevenueCat dashboard for both stores; consider failing closed or retrying rather than showing a coming-soon state.
findings.validation: Launch the paywall on a sandbox account and confirm real packages render
findings.owner_confirmation_required: RevenueCat dashboard must have the 'premium' entitlement and a live offering configured for both App Store and Play.

findings.title: Signed release AAB is verified but not shippable — README's release command omits the required dart-defines
findings.evidence: README.md 'Play Store Build' documents `flutter build appbundle --release` with no dart-defines. The AAB built with that exact command installs and launches on Android 16 but lands on _ConfigurationErrorApp: 'Uygulama yapılandırması eksik — Supabase, RevenueCat ayarları bu üretim derlemesine eklenmemiş.' (screenshot 30_release_smoke_01.png). AppConfig.validateForRelease (app_config.dart) returns issues for supabase and revenueCat, and main.dart:109-119 swaps in the error app. The correct command IS documented elsewhere: docs/YAYIN_ADIMLARI.md:171 and docs/android_signing_setup.md:70 both specify --dart-define-from-file=.env.mobile.release.json. Only .env.mobile.release.example.json exists on this machine.
findings.reproduction: flutter build appbundle --release ; install the resulting AAB and launch
findings.expected: The documented release command produces a shippable binary
findings.actual: It produces a binary that boots into the configuration-error screen
findings.impact: Following README alone yields a non-shippable AAB. The runtime guard behaves correctly — this is a documentation inconsistency, not a code defect.
findings.root_cause: README's Play Store Build section was not kept in sync with YAYIN_ADIMLARI.md when dart-define-based release config was introduced.
findings.remediation: 1) cp .env.mobile.release.example.json .env.mobile.release.json and fill real SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, REVENUECAT_API_KEY_ANDROID, REVENUECAT_API_KEY_IOS (gitignored). 2) flutter build appbundle --release --dart-define-from-file=.env.mobile.release.json. 3) Align README's Play Store Build section with YAYIN_ADIMLARI.md.
findings.validation: Rebuild with the dart-define file, install, and confirm the app reaches onboarding/home instead of the configuration-error screen
findings.note: Values were NOT hard-coded and release validation was NOT disabled (Phase 2 rule 10 / stop condition 7).
findings.phase3_update: 2026-08-02 (Phase 3): Scoped search of all permitted local sources found SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (in the gitignored .env.web.release.json; both hash-identical to the bundled defaults in app_config.dart, i.e. the same production project and a publishable/public key). REVENUECAT_API_KEY_ANDROID and REVENUECAT_API_KEY_IOS are MISSING everywhere: no env file, no shell env var, no Keychain entry, and the old project copies under ~/Downloads contain no .env.mobile.release.json. Per rules 7/10 and stop condition 1 no placeholder values were invented, .env.mobile.release.json was NOT created, and validateForRelease was not weakened. The production-config Android AAB, Android smoke, and iOS config build therefore remain BLOCKED. README was corrected (see commit docs(release)). Independent re-confirmation: the Phase 2 release APK set still installed on the Android 16 emulator boots into _ConfigurationErrorApp.

findings.title: Shop sells the 600-coin Neon frame but the server spend_coins allowlist rejects it — the purchase can never succeed
findings.status: FIXED — migration written (owner must apply to production)
findings.evidence: Full chain traced. shop_items seed contains ('avatar_frame_neon', ..., 600, ...) in supabase/2026-07-23_shop_items_sync.sql:52-55 and 2026-07-13_shop_chat_suggestions.sql:51. The UI lists it at 600 coins (shop_screen.dart:174-183) and includes it in _supportedItemIds (shop_screen.dart:141-145), whose own comment states that membership means the product actually does something. Purchase calls spendCoins(600,'purchase_avatar_frame_neon') (shop_screen.dart:465-468). The server allowlist in supabase/2026-07-29_shop_purchase_integrity_fix.sql:105-116 permits only spin_wheel_extra, avatar_frame_gold and profile_badge_vip, returning {'success':false,'error':'product not available'}. No later migration adds avatar_frame_neon (the 'product not available' guard exists in exactly one file). spendCoins discards the error string and returns bool (supabase_zankurd_repository.dart:943-959), so the UI shows the generic K.purchaseFailed (shop_screen.dart:487-489). Client-side rendering WAS fixed on 2026-07-31 (AvatarFrame.neon exists and avatar_editor_screen.dart:69-70,98 unlocks it via hasPurchased) but can never trigger.
findings.impact: A user with 600+ earned coins sees an advertised cosmetic, taps buy, and receives a permanent unexplained failure. Coins are not deducted, but the product is unobtainable.
findings.remediation: Forward-only migration adding 'avatar_frame_neon' to the spend_coins allowlist; additionally propagate the server error string through spendCoins so the UI can explain failures.
findings.validation: RPC contract test plus a real 600-coin purchase; the frame must then be selectable in the avatar editor.

findings.title: Quiz answer tiles paint white text on correct/wrong gradients at 2.97:1 and 3.73:1 — below WCAG AA
findings.evidence: Measured with the WCAG relative-luminance formula. correct #3DA968 -> #2D8250 and wrong #E5533D -> #C53F2B (app_theme.dart:486-487,672-682); text is Colors.white when correct/wrong (quiz_option_tile.dart:114-116). White on gradient start: correct 2.97:1, wrong 3.73:1; midpoints 3.75:1 and 4.35:1; ends 4.75:1 and 5.10:1. Label is fontSize 15 (compact) or 17 at FontWeight.w800 (quiz_option_tile.dart:241-244); WCAG large-text bold threshold is 14pt = 18.67px, so 17px does NOT qualify and the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold applies. Both gradients are static const and the text colour is a fixed Colors.white, so the ratio is identical in light and dark themes — confirmed on device. No test covers this: contrast_policy_test.dart measures only brand orange, heroScrim and the gold band; quiz_accent_test.dart asserts gradient identity only (:109-115); no test anywhere calls contrastRatio against the answer states.
findings.impact: Answer text on the app's most-viewed surface is below the AA readability threshold for low-vision users. Mitigated for discriminability (persistent check/cross icons, shake, semantics text) but not for legibility.
findings.remediation: Darken both gradients so every stop reaches >=4.5:1 against white (lowest-risk, keeps brand hue); or add a scrim behind the text; or raise the label to >=18.67px to fall under the 3:1 large-text threshold.
findings.validation: Add contrastRatio(Colors.white, <stop>) >= 4.5 assertions for both ends of both gradients to contrast_policy_test.dart.

findings.title: Leaderboard pushed from the quiz result renders with no Material ancestor — all text draws with fallback yellow underlines and there is no back control
findings.evidence: quiz_result_screen.dart:1127-1131 pushes LeaderboardScreen via AppRoute. LeaderboardScreen has no Scaffold, no AppBar and no PopScope — only SafeArea (leaderboard_screen.dart:255,466); as tab 2 the Scaffold comes from AppShell (app_shell.dart:287). Verified on a real Android 16 emulator through the full flow (quiz -> result -> 'Rêzbendî'): every string renders in Flutter's DefaultTextStyle.fallback() style with yellow double underlines and wrong typography. That fallback is NOT debug-only; it renders the same in release. Android system back does pop the route (verified), so Android users are not trapped. On iOS there is no back control AND no edge-swipe: AppRoute is a plain PageRouteBuilder (app_route.dart:4) and the repo contains no pageTransitionsTheme, CupertinoPageTransitionsBuilder or CupertinoPageRoute (grep: 0 hits) — so the screen would be inescapable. The iOS sub-claim is source-verified only; not run on device.
findings.impact: A user reaching the leaderboard from the quiz result sees a visually broken screen. On iOS there is additionally no way back.
findings.remediation: Wrap the pushed usage in Scaffold(appBar: ...) or give LeaderboardScreen an isEmbedded flag so it supplies its own Scaffold when presented as a full route. Separately, adding pageTransitionsTheme with CupertinoPageTransitionsBuilder restores iOS swipe-back app-wide.
findings.validation: On device: quiz -> result -> leaderboard shows normal typography, a visible back control, and iOS edge-swipe works.
findings.confidence: high (render) / medium-high (iOS inescapability — source proven, device test NOT RUN)

findings.title: 'Remove photo' clears the profile column but never deletes the Storage object, which stays publicly readable at a deterministic path
findings.evidence: uploadAvatarPhoto writes to the fixed path '${user.id}/avatar.$ext' with upsert:true in the avatars bucket (supabase_zankurd_repository.dart:284-301). The bucket is created with public=true and the policy "Avatar photos are publicly readable" using (bucket_id='avatars') — readable by anon (2026-07-05_avatar_showcase.sql:27-46). A remove action exists (ValueKey('avatar-remove-photo') -> clearPhoto:true, avatar_editor_screen.dart:239-246) but only nulls profiles.avatar_url. There is NO storage remove/delete call anywhere in lib/ (grep: 0 hits), so the object persists at a guessable public URL. Changing extension (png -> jpg) also orphans the previous object. IMPORTANT MITIGATION: account deletion DOES purge storage — delete from storage.objects where bucket_id='avatars' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = v_user_id::text (2026-07-05_avatar_showcase.sql:169-171) — so the store-mandated deletion path is correct.
findings.impact: A user who removes their photo reasonably believes it is gone; it remains publicly retrievable. Bounded because account deletion does clean up.
findings.remediation: Call client.storage.from('avatars').remove([path]) on removal and on extension-changing re-upload; clear the profile URL only after a successful delete and surface failures.
findings.validation: Mock storage adapter contract test asserting remove() is invoked on the removal path.

findings.title: Avatar photos are an unmoderated image-UGC surface shown to strangers — no filter, no report, and blocking does not hide them
findings.status: FIXED — client + migration written (owner must apply)
findings.evidence: Avatars of other players are rendered on the leaderboard (leaderboard_screen.dart:938,1168 via entry.avatarUrl), in matchmaking against the opponent (matchmaking_screen.dart:415,515,1168), in room chat and in the tournament bracket; avatar_url is selected for other players in supabase_zankurd_repository.dart:731,1176,1236,1260. Filtering: none — the bucket enforces only MIME type (jpeg/png/webp) and a 2 MB limit; ChatModerationPolicy is text-only and is invoked at exactly one call site (room_chat.dart:148). Reporting: none — report_room_message covers chat messages only; there is no path to report an avatar. Blocking: block_player filters chat, but the leaderboard and matchmaking queries carry no blocked-user filter, so a blocked user's avatar keeps appearing. Published contact exists.
findings.policy_reference: App Store Review Guideline 1.2 (filter / report / block / published contact); Google Play UGC policy
findings.impact: Three of Apple's four UGC requirements are unmet for the avatar surface, which is visible to strangers.
findings.remediation: Add an avatar report flow (extend the existing message_reports pattern); exclude blocked users' avatars server-side or hide them client-side; add post-upload moderation or automated NSFW scanning; provide an admin path to disable an avatar.
findings.validation: Report and block flows reachable from any surface showing another user's avatar; blocked user's avatar absent from leaderboard and matchmaking.

findings.title: Display names pass no profanity or impersonation filter on any client path and have no server-side validation at all
findings.status: FIXED — client + migration written (owner must apply)
findings.evidence: Client validation is length-only: name.length < 2 and name.length > 24 (profile_name_gate_screen.dart:323,326). ChatModerationPolicy is referenced in exactly one place in the whole repo — room_chat.dart:148 — and is never applied to names. No server-side display_name CHECK constraint, trigger or validating RPC exists in any migration (all supabase/*.sql scanned). updateProfileName writes straight through (supabase_zankurd_repository.dart:219 and :149 'display_name'). Names appear to strangers on the leaderboard, in rooms, matchmaking and chat, and there is no way to report a name.
findings.policy_reference: App Store Review Guideline 1.2; Google Play UGC policy
findings.impact: Any user can set an abusive or impersonating display name (e.g. a support/admin identity) that is broadcast to strangers.
findings.remediation: Apply a name-specific moderation policy on all three client write paths AND enforce it server-side (trigger or CHECK), since a client-only filter is trivially bypassed; add a protected-name list and a report-a-name path.
findings.validation: Server rejects a profane or protected name submitted directly via the REST API, not just via the UI.
